title: Peking Duck

seo.title: Authentic Peking Duck Recipe | Crispy Skin at Home
seo.metaDescription: Master the art of making authentic Peking Duck at home with our step-by-step recipe. Achieve crispy skin and tender meat for a truly unforgettable Chinese dinner.
seo.h1: Authentic Peking Duck Recipe: Crispy Skin, Tender Meat
h2Headings: Tips for Perfect Crispy Peking Duck
seo.imageAlt: A whole roasted authentic Peking Duck with crispy skin, served with pancakes, scallions, and hoisin sauce.
seo.imageCaption: Achieve restaurant-quality authentic Peking Duck at home with our detailed recipe, perfect for a special occasion!

description: Peking Duck is a legendary Chinese dish renowned for its incredibly crispy skin and succulent, tender meat. Traditionally served with thin pancakes, fresh scallions, and a rich hoisin sauce, it offers a delightful textural and flavor experience. This recipe guides you to recreate this iconic banquet dish in your own kitchen, perfect for impressing guests.

instructions.title: Prepare the Duck
instructions.text: Thoroughly clean the whole duck, removing any excess fat and giblets. Pat the duck completely dry inside and out with paper towels. Puncture the skin all over with a fork, being careful not to pierce the meat.

instructions.title: Blanch and Glaze the Skin
instructions.text: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Carefully pour the boiling water all over the duck skin, ensuring even coverage. This helps to tighten the skin. In a small bowl, whisk together honey, rice vinegar, soy sauce, five-spice powder, grated ginger, and minced garlic to create the glaze. Generously brush the glaze all over the duck skin.

instructions.title: Air Dry the Duck
instructions.text: This step is crucial for crispy skin. Place the glazed duck on a rack set over a baking sheet. Refrigerate uncovered for at least 6-8 hours, or ideally overnight (12-24 hours). Ensure good air circulation around the duck to dry the skin completely.

instructions.title: Preheat Oven and Roast
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 375F (190C). Place the air-dried duck breast-side up on a roasting rack in a large roasting pan. Pour 1 cup of water into the bottom of the roasting pan. Roast for 1 hour, then reduce the oven temperature to 325F (160C) and continue roasting for another 1 to 1.5 hours, or until the internal temperature reaches 165F (74C) in the thickest part of the thigh.

instructions.title: Crisp the Skin and Rest
instructions.text: Once the duck is cooked through, increase the oven temperature to 400F (200C). Roast for an additional 15-20 minutes, or until the skin is deeply golden brown and very crispy. Keep a close eye to prevent burning. Remove the duck from the oven and let it rest on a cutting board for at least 15-20 minutes before carving. This allows the juices to redistribute.

instructions.title: Carve and Serve
instructions.text: Carefully carve the crispy skin and tender meat into thin slices. Arrange the duck slices on a serving platter. Serve immediately with warm thin pancakes, julienned scallions, julienned cucumber, and hoisin sauce for guests to assemble their own delicious wraps.

tips: For truly crispy skin, air-drying the duck for at least 6-8 hours, or preferably overnight, is the most critical step. This removes moisture, allowing the skin to crisp up perfectly.
While a whole duck is traditional, for a quicker version, you can adapt this recipe to duck breasts, though the skin crispiness will differ. Ensure to render the fat thoroughly.
Serve Peking Duck immediately after carving to enjoy the skin at its crispiest. Reheat leftover duck meat gently, but the skin will not retain its original crunch.
